Subject: Reserved Dedicated Capacity — anchor pricing & phased start plan for Helix AI

Hi Helen,

Thanks again for the conversation yesterday. Per our discussion, I wanted to put a concise starter proposal on paper so your procurement team has something to react to. High-level summary below:

- Commitment: 24-month reserved commit (option to extend at renewal)
- Anchor size: 40 A100-equivalent GPU pool (baseline throughput target: 120 qps for embedding-heavy workloads; token-latency SLOs to be specified in SOW)
- Pricing: $X/unit-month with a 20% anchor discount for the first 6 months, moving to 12% thereafter — proposed to reflect the staged uptake you described
- Ramp: soft-start (month 0–3): 40% of pool available; month 4–6: 70%; month 7: 100% live capacity
- Start date: target capacity start window: 2027-06-01 — flexible by up to 30 days with a credit ladder for delayed availability

I attached a short term sheet (RDW-5421_pricing_term_sheet_v1.pdf) and a suggested ramp calendar. Can your procurement team confirm whether a 24-month term with the proposed staged discount ladder is acceptable, or whether Helix prefers 12/36 options for comparison?

If helpful, happy to run a short 30-min walkthrough of the ramp calendar with your ops team next week.

Best,
Olga Petrov
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Attachment: RDW-5421_pricing_term_sheet_v1.pdf (PDF, 2 pages)

Hi Olga — thanks for the clear summary. A few quick clarifying questions from procurement and our platform team:

1) Can you provide the equivalent monthly committed GPU hours and an estimate of average token cost at the anchor rate? Procurement needs line-item clarity for our CAPEX planning.
2) On ramp: the team is nervous about a hard 7-month path to 100%. Can we propose a slightly longer ramp (9 months) with a smaller early-month credit so we don’t pay full-rate before we see production traffic?
3) Would Redwood consider a 36-month option in exchange for an increased upfront discount and a firm SLA credit (e.g., 5% service credit if latency SLO missed more than X days)?

We ran this by ops and they asked for a more prescriptive start-gate definition — what metrics trigger moving from soft-start to full capacity?

Helen

- Monthly committed GPU hours: at 40 A100-e qpool this maps to ~28,800 GPU-hours/month (estimate; exact depends on instance type and utilization profile). We’ll provide a line-item calc in the term sheet next revision.
- Ramp extension: 9-month ramp is reasonable; we can move to a 9-month phased calendar and replace the initial 6-month 20% discount with a stepped-credit ladder (example attached).
- 36-month option: we can offer an extended-term structure — proposed: 25% upfront discount for the first 9 months + a 7% ongoing discount vs default 24-month pricing, in exchange for a 36-month minimum and a strengthened SLA credit schedule. Ben, can you add the SLA-credit thresholds in the next doc?

Hi all — attaching two options in brief (see attached spreadsheets):

Option A — 24-month (recommended for balance):
- Anchor: 40 A100-e GPUs
- Pricing: $9,600/month per A100-e equivalent (anchor 20% off month 1–6, 12% months 7–24)
- Ramp: 9-month phased activation (40% m0–m2, 55% m3–m5, 80% m6, 100% m7–m9)
- SLA credits: standard (3% credit tier for sustained latency breaches >3 days; escalations handled by customer success)

Option B — 36-month (volume trade):
- Anchor: 40 A100-e GPUs
- Pricing: $8,900/month per A100-e equivalent (25% upfront for months 1–9 then 7% ongoing)
- Ramp: 6–9 month configurable (we propose 9 months given your production constraints)
- SLA credits: firmed-up 5% credit for severity-level incidents meeting defined thresholds; requires sign-off of SLO appendix

Notes: We can add a delayed-availability credit ladder (credit % tied to days beyond agreed start-date) if that helps reduce your upfront exposure.

Attachments: Helix_phase_ramp_calendar.xlsx (Excel), RDW-5421_pricing_term_sheet_v1.pdf (revised line items)

Thanks,

Principal, Sales — Enterprise
Redwood Inference

Ben/Olga — appreciate the fast follow and the breakouts. Procurement + Finance reviewed Option B (36-month) and have signaled they prefer the deeper rate if Redwood will: 1) confirm the 9-month ramp as binding in the SOW; 2) include a delayed-start credit ladder with a cap; and 3) commit to the 5% SLA credit language.

Assuming those three items are formalized, Helix is prepared to proceed on Option B. Please send an NDA/SOW/DocuSign packet and we will loop legal for final redlines. I will expect a DocuSign link and an updated term sheet that includes the ramp calendar and the SLO appendix.
